attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter post, stated in his own voice and not quoting anyone else.

semantics.note: The normalised claim keeps all three parts: every company loses money, data centers 'seemingly' behind schedule, and the vast majority not under construction. 'Seemingly' hedges the delay part, so that part is an impression and cannot be scored. 'Every company' may be hyperbole, but it reads as a factual universal.

contract.note: The plain reading (generative-AI firms, net loss, project-count majority) is ordinary. The contract demands an accounting basis and a set period before scoring the loss claim. That is strict, but it is applied evenly to both sides. Who counts as 'every company' and the 'vast majority' threshold are evaluator choices, so the result depends on them.

evidence.note: Sightline report dated 2026-02-24. Of about 16GW slated for 2026, about 11GW (roughly two-thirds) shows no construction. It measures capacity in large projects, not a project-count share of all announced AI projects, so it cannot settle 'vast majority'.

Contemporaneous reporting: 26% of 2025 projects slipped, and 30-50% of 2026 capacity may be delayed. These are forecast risk and partial lateness, and they do not falsify a qualified 'seemingly' impression.

A secondary report, based on a founder interview, that Midjourney is profitable. The profit measure and period are unspecified, and this is the company describing itself. It is material counter-context, but under the contract it does not settle a profitable company for Oct–Dec 2025.

Anthropic's audited filing (available 2026-10-26, before the cutoff) shows net losses every year, including 2025. It is a single company's annual figure, not the selected quarter or the whole population.

reviews.rationale: The loss claim cannot be tested: the company population is undefined and there are no comparable accounts. Midjourney's reported profit lacks a basis and period, and Anthropic's losses cover only one company. The construction claim has only capacity data (about two-thirds of 2026 GW unstarted), not a project count. The delay claim is a hedged impression. The packet settles none of the three parts.
